title: 'replies' feature
description:
I'm interested in creating a 'replies' capability so that agents can efficiently poll the backend for new replies to comments, so that they can process followups.

if it's possible to query this in the API: search comments newer than given datetime from all tasks in the project, and store a 'last reply' file in the local directory to track the datetime.

alternatively, vikunja has a notifications feature we could leverage.

title: to/from markdown
description: I think models prefer markdown because it's terse. add --md in some places to convert between md and html. (md -> html for setters, html -> md for getters). can use pandoc for this or a rust thing if there's an okay one. okay to fail if pandoc is missing.

title: expose 'in progress' state
description:
I think we currently have --done true/false

can you make this --done todo/doing/done? (unless the 'doing' state is already exposed somewhere else)

there are few enough vik users that I'm okay breaking backwards compat here

comments.author: Abe Winter
comments.text: Done. Vikunja has no native in-progress field, so 'doing' maps onto percent_done: todo = not done & 0%, doing = not done & >0%, done = done. --done now takes todo/doing/done (clap value enum) on both 'list' (filter) and 'modify' (setter); 'modify --done doing' sets percent_done=0.5 unless --percent-done overrides. Note: this drops the old combined 'not done' (todo+doing) value — use --filter 'done = false' for that (AGENTS.sample.md updated). Verified live against project 15.

title: permission error when user doesn't have access to a project
description:
when I call `vik list` on a project I have no access to, I get an empty list rather than an error. is there any way to know this from the API response and print an error message instead?

(you can use project 8 as a project the test user doesn't have permission to access)

comments.author: Abe Winter
comments.text: Real. /tasks?filter=project_id=N returns 200 [] whether the project is empty OR inaccessible, hiding permission errors. Fix: when the task list comes back empty, probe GET /projects/{id} (new client.project_accessible) — 403/404 -> bail with 'no access to project N (it may not exist, or your token lacks permission)'. Only adds a request in the empty case; genuinely-empty accessible projects still return []. Verified: project 8 now errors (exit 1), project 14/15 unaffected.

title: (manual) dedicated testing account
description: dedicated project + user on test server

title: claiming a task is consistently weird
description: for `vik modify --mine`, I've gotten complaints that the json output is not helpful (which is tolerable) but also that it returns exit code 2 on success. can you replicate this and if real, fix?

comments.author: Abe Winter
comments.text: Reproduced the core issue (saw exit 1, not exactly 2): 'vik modify --mine' on a task you already hold 400s with Vikunja code 4021 'already assigned', so re-claiming failed nonzero. Also the output was the terse assignee-PUT body {Created, user_id}. Fix: treat 4021 as idempotent success, and return the full task instead. Now re-claiming exits 0 and prints the task. Verified live on task 39.

title: getter for comments
description: in some cases comments will be used in a pseudo chat style, which means the agent needs to read them. can you add a comments getter for tasks?

comments.author: Abe Winter
comments.text: Added 'vik comments <task>' -> GET /tasks/{id}/comments, returns the comment array (id, comment, author, created). Mirrors comment(add)/comments(list) like attach/attachments.

title: compact mode
description:
--compact flag to the `list` command which produces fewer fields to save context (we will need to think about which fields to keep) this is a sample response: { "assignees": [ { "created": "2026-06-28T21:25:58Z", "id": 1, "name": "", "updated": "2026-06-28T21:25:58Z", "username": "awinter" } ], "attachments": null, "bucket_id": 0, "cover_image_attachment_id": 0, "created": "2026-06-28T22:04:37Z", "created_by": { "created": "2026-06-28T21:25:58Z", "id": 1, "name": "", "updated": "2026-06-28T21:25:58Z", "username": "awinter" }, "description": "

(user does this manually)

", "done": false, "done_at": "0001-01-01T00:00:00Z", "due_date": "0001-01-01T00:00:00Z", "end_date": "0001-01-01T00:00:00Z", "hex_color": "", "id": 4, "identifier": "#4", "index": 4, "is_favorite": false, "labels": null, "percent_done": 0, "position": 0, "priority": 0, "project_id": 4, "reactions": null, "related_tasks": {}, "reminders": null, "repeat_after": 0, "repeat_mode": 0, "start_date": "0001-01-01T00:00:00Z", "title": "decide on sim approach and describe initial test layout", "updated": "2026-06-28T22:05:51Z" } I think key fields are title, description, assignee.username, id, attachments, related_tasks.*.{id, title}, priority. open to suggestions here too.

comments.author: Abe Winter
comments.text: Added 'list --compact'. Projects each task to: id, title, done (always), priority (if !=0), description (if non-empty), assignees->[username], attachments->[{id,name}], related_tasks->{kind:[{id,title}]}. Drops empty/zero/null fields (the raw response is mostly unset date columns). Applied after --topo-sort so ordering+trimming compose. 2 unit tests incl. the sample task from this issue.

title: sort by blockers
description:
can you add a --topo-sort flag to tasks that does a topological sort (likely on the client side) to show tasks in blocker order, with task ID as a tie breaker?

(I'm open to other cli approaches for specify this if topo sort is built in to vikunja or there's a more idiomatic way to get it)

comments.author: Abe Winter
comments.text: Implemented --topo-sort on list. Client-side Kahn topo sort over the returned set: blockers first, task id as tie-break. Edges from each task's related_tasks (blocking => this-before-that, blocked => that-before-this); relations to tasks outside the page are ignored; cycles broken by id order so nothing drops. 6 unit tests cover id-only, both relation directions, chain+tiebreak, out-of-set, and cycle. NOT live-tested (no token this session). OPEN QUESTION: needs confirmation that GET /tasks populates related_tasks in the list response (the expand param doesn't cover relations). If it doesn't, we'd need a per-task GET /tasks/{id}/relations pass.

title: file attachments and embeds
description:
add the ability to:
- attach files to a task
- embed images in the markdown description

(not sure if either / both of these are possible, obv ignore if not)

comments.author: Abe Winter
comments.text: Done & verified live. Commands: attach <task> <file>... (multipart PUT /tasks/{id}/attachments), attachments <task> (GET list), attach --embed (upload then append ![name](/api/v1/tasks/{id}/attachments/{aid}) to description). Upload returns {errors,success:[attachment...]}. Embed URL is a relative /api/v1 path the frontend resolves. NB: also fixed a modify bug surfaced here — Vikunja POST /tasks zeroes omitted value fields (done/priority), so modify+embed now read-merge-write the full task. Docs updated.

title: implement list, modify, comment, create commands
description:
use terminology from the API for verb and flag names. the initial implementation should be minimal, i.e. doesn't need to allow all API fields in the CLI

don't do file attachments yet in this stage (guessing it will be a bit of a can of worms)

comments.author: Abe Winter
comments.text: Done & verified live against a real instance (project 13). Commands: list (--done/--filter/--sort-by/--order-by/-s/--per-page, GET /tasks w/ project_id filter), create (PUT /projects/{id}/tasks, --description - = stdin), modify (partial POST /tasks/{id} + --assignee via PUT assignees), comment (PUT comments, - = stdin). Fixes from live testing: default https:// when server omits scheme; graceful error when --assignee username needs /users scope the token lacks (numeric id works). Attachments deferred to vik-eev.4.

title: create barebones rust cli project
description:
cargo init or whatever, plus the API client. unless we use a generator from a spec, only implement the methods we need (see README.md)

also do the config file format in this phase

and if the CLI framework supports env var overrides (like viper does in golang), use that for VIKUNJA_TOKEN, and allow it to be passed by CLI param as well

comments.author: Abe Winter
comments.text: Scaffold done & building. clap v4 (--server/--token/--project/--config, token via VIKUNJA_TOKEN env, flag>env>config). config.rs discovers .vikunja.yaml/vikunja.yaml in cwd then $HOME. client.rs = reqwest blocking + bearer auth + raw-JSON get/put_json/post_json + resolve_project/resolve_user. 'vik projects' smoke command works (help + clean no-config error verified). Sandbox notes: needed --read /usr (exec for gcc collect2/cc1) and a writable TMPDIR; latter pinned via .cargo/config.toml. Live API call untested pending a server+token.

title: outline rust approach
description:
make decisions about:
- what CLI framework to use
- if relevant, how to consume openapi specs into a client

post the answers as a comment on this task

comments.author: Abe Winter
comments.text:
Approach decided — full writeup in docs/design.md.

- CLI framework: clap v4 (derive). Env override via #[arg(env="VIKUNJA_TOKEN")];
  flag > env > config precedence. Global --server/--project/--config/--token.
- OpenAPI: NO generator. Spec is Swagger 2.0 (progenitor needs 3.x) and we need
  ~10 of 126 endpoints. Hand-write a small typed reqwest client + a few serde
  structs; keep docs/vikunja-swagger.json as reference.
- HTTP: reqwest blocking + json,multipart,rustls-tls (no async runtime, no OpenSSL).
- serde/serde_json; partial updates via Option + skip_serializing_if.
- Config: serde_yaml, discover ./.vikunja.yaml|vikunja.yaml then $HOME; fields
  username/server/project; project name->id resolved via GET /projects.
- anyhow for errors; raw JSON to stdout (pipe to jq); --description - reads stdin.
- Layout: main.rs / config.rs / client.rs / models.rs / commands.rs.

title: get vikunja API docs
description:
ideally from an openapi spec, failing that from a docs page or reading their code

focus on the features described in the readme

comments.author: Abe Winter
comments.text:
API docs captured in docs/vikunja-api.md (+ raw spec docs/vikunja-swagger.json).

Key facts:
- Swagger 2.0, base {server}/api/v1. Auth: 'Authorization: Bearer <VIKUNJA_TOKEN>'.
- list:   GET /tasks?filter=project_id = <id>[ && done = false]&sort_by=&order_by= (returns []Task; status is the 'done' bool, not an enum)
- create: PUT /projects/{id}/tasks  body models.Task (title required)
- modify: POST /tasks/{id}          partial models.Task (done, title, priority, ...)
- owner:  PUT /tasks/{taskID}/assignees {user_id}  (resolve username via GET /users?s=)
- comment:PUT /tasks/{taskID}/comments {comment}
- attach: PUT /tasks/{id}/attachments  multipart form field 'files' (vik-eev.4)
- resolve config project name->id via GET /projects.

Decision: list via global /tasks + project_id filter rather than the view-scoped
/projects/{id}/views/{view}/tasks, to avoid a view-discovery round-trip.
